stories.title: Hiding in the Garden
stories.note: The serpent's trick and the wrong choice are told simply. Death is not mentioned to the youngest; the story ends with God's care.

panels.lambs: God made a beautiful garden, and Adam and Eve lived there with all the animals.
panels.lions: God planted a garden in Eden, full of trees with good fruit and a river running through it. He put Adam there, and He gave him Eve. Animals of every kind lived there too.

panels.lambs: God told them: you may eat from every tree, but not from this one.
panels.lions: In the middle of the garden stood one special tree. God told Adam that they could eat from every tree in the garden, except that one.

panels.lambs: A sneaky serpent tried to trick Eve.
panels.lions: One day the serpent, the sneakiest animal of all, came to Eve. “Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” he asked. He wanted her to stop trusting God.

panels.lambs: Eve and Adam ate the fruit. Then they felt sad and afraid.
panels.lions: Eve looked at the fruit. It looked so good. She ate some and gave some to Adam, and he ate too. Straight away they knew they had done wrong, and they made coverings out of fig leaves.

panels.lambs: They hid. But God called, “Where art thou?”
panels.lions: In the cool of the day they heard God in the garden, and they hid among the trees. But God called to Adam, “Where art thou?” God knew where they were. He came looking for them.

panels.lambs: God still cared for them. He made them warm coats to wear.
panels.lions: Adam and Eve had to leave the garden. But God did not stop caring for them. He made them coats of skins and dressed them Himself.

verse.text: And the LORD God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?
verse.plain: God always comes looking for us, even when we hide.

items.label: the special tree with golden fruit

ask: Why do you think Adam and Eve hid?
What can you do when you have done something wrong?
talk.do: Play hide-and-seek. Whoever finds the other says, “Where art thou?”
talk.pray: Dear God, thank You that You always find me. When I do wrong, help me come to You and say sorry.

stories.title: Gideon's Three Hundred Men
stories.note: The enemy simply run away. The fighting in Judges 7:22 is left out.

panels.lambs: Gideon was hiding while he worked. He was afraid.
panels.lions: The Midianites kept coming to take Israel's food. Gideon was so afraid of them that he beat out his wheat inside a winepress, where nobody would see him.

panels.lambs: A messenger from God said, “The LORD is with thee.”
panels.lions: Then the angel of the LORD came and sat under an oak tree. He said to Gideon, “The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.” Gideon did not feel mighty at all!

panels.lambs: Gideon asked for a sign. The fleece was wet, and the ground was dry!
panels.lions: Gideon wanted to be sure. He laid a woolly fleece on the ground at night, and asked God to make the fleece wet but the ground dry. In the morning he squeezed a whole bowl of water out of the fleece, and the ground was dry.

panels.lambs: God said Gideon had too many men. Only 300 could stay.
panels.lions: Gideon gathered a big army. But God said, “The people that are with thee are too many”. God wanted everyone to know that the help came from Him. In the end only 300 men stayed: the ones who lapped up water from their hands.

panels.lambs: At night the 300 held trumpets, and jars with lamps inside.
panels.lions: In the middle of the night the 300 crept up around the enemy camp. Each man held a trumpet, and a clay jar with a lamp hidden inside.

panels.lambs: They blew the trumpets and shone the lamps, and the enemy ran away!
panels.lions: Gideon blew his trumpet. All 300 broke their jars, held up their shining lamps, blew their trumpets and shouted, “The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon.” The Midianites were so frightened that they all ran away!

verse.text: The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.
verse.plain: Even when you feel small and afraid, God is with you and makes you brave.

talk.pray: Dear God, when I feel small, thank You that You are with me. Help me be brave.

stories.title: Where You Go, I Will Go
stories.note: Naomi's husband and sons have died; the story says so once, gently, for the older children only.

panels.lambs: Naomi was going home. Orpah said goodbye, but Ruth stayed.
panels.lions: Naomi's husband and her two sons had died in the land of Moab, and she decided to go home to Bethlehem. Her sons' wives, Orpah and Ruth, set out with her. Orpah kissed Naomi goodbye and went back. But Ruth held on tight.

panels.lambs: Ruth hugged Naomi and said, “whither thou goest, I will go.”
panels.lions: Ruth said to Naomi, “whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge.” She loved Naomi, and she would trust Naomi's God too.

panels.lambs: They walked all the way to Bethlehem.
panels.lions: So the two of them walked all the way to Bethlehem. They arrived just as the barley harvest was beginning.

panels.lambs: Ruth picked up barley in the field to make bread.
panels.lions: They needed food, so Ruth went to glean: to pick up the stalks of barley the reapers left behind. The field she came to belonged to a man named Boaz.

panels.lambs: Kind Boaz shared his food and left extra barley for Ruth.
panels.lions: Boaz was kind. At mealtime he gave Ruth bread and roasted grain, and he told his workers to drop extra handfuls of barley on purpose, just for her.

panels.lambs: Ruth and Boaz married and had a baby boy. Naomi was so happy!
panels.lions: Later Boaz married Ruth, and God gave them a baby boy called Obed. Naomi held him on her lap. Her empty home was full of love again.

verse.text: whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge
verse.plain: Ruth promised to stay with Naomi and to trust Naomi's God. Real friends stick together.

Who could you be kind to, the way Boaz was kind to Ruth?
talk.do: Share a snack with someone today, the way Boaz shared with Ruth.
talk.pray: Dear God, help me be a loyal friend like Ruth, and kind like Boaz.

stories.title: The Fourth Man in the Fire
stories.note: The soldiers who died at the furnace door (Daniel 3:22) are left out. The fourth man is described as the king saw him, without saying who He was.

panels.lambs: King Nebuchadnezzar made a giant gold statue. Everyone had to bow down to it.
panels.lions: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon set up a giant statue of gold on the plain of Dura. When the music played, everyone had to fall down and worship it.

panels.lambs: But three friends would not bow. They only worshipped God.
panels.lions: The music played and everybody bowed, except three young men: Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego. They would only worship God.

panels.lambs: The king was cross. The friends said, “our God whom we serve is able to deliver us.”
panels.lions: The king was very cross. He said he would throw them into a burning furnace. But the friends answered bravely, “our God whom we serve is able to deliver us.”

panels.lambs: So the king's soldiers took them to a big, hot furnace.
panels.lions: The king had the furnace made seven times hotter than usual. His soldiers tied up the three friends and put them into the fire.

panels.lambs: But in the fire there were four men, walking, and not hurt!
panels.lions: Then the king jumped up in surprise. “Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt,” he said. Someone was in the fire with them!

panels.lambs: The friends came out safe. Not one hair was burnt!
panels.lions: The king called them out, and out they came. Their hair was not burnt, their coats were not scorched, and they did not even smell of smoke! The king said, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego.”

verse.text: our God whom we serve is able to deliver us
verse.plain: God is strong enough to save the people who trust Him, even in a fire.

ask: How do you think the three friends felt when they said no to the king?
When is it hard for you to do what is right?
talk.do: Hold hands and name one person who needs to be brave this week.
talk.pray: Dear God, You are with me even when things are hard. Help me be brave and do what is right.

stories.title: Teach Us to Pray
stories.note: Jesus' picture-stories are told as stories He told. The Lord's Prayer is quoted in the KJV words of Luke 11.

panels.lambs: Jesus was praying. His friends watched Him.
panels.lions: One day Jesus was praying. When He finished, His disciples came to Him.

panels.lambs: One said, “Lord, teach us to pray.”
panels.lions: One of them said, “Lord, teach us to pray.” So Jesus taught them a prayer that begins, “Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.”

panels.lambs: Jesus told a story: a man knocked on his friend's door at midnight.
panels.lions: Then Jesus told a story. A man had a visitor arrive late at night, and he had no food to give him. So at midnight he went to his friend's house and knocked: “Friend, lend me three loaves”.

panels.lambs: He kept on asking, and his friend gave him the bread.
panels.lions: His friend called from inside, “Trouble me not”. The door was shut and the children were in bed. But the man kept on knocking and asking, until his friend got up and gave him as much as he needed.

panels.lambs: Jesus said, “Ask, and it shall be given you.”
panels.lions: Jesus said, “Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.”

panels.lambs: God is a good Father. He loves to give good things to His children.
panels.lions: If a child asks his father for a fish, will he give him a snake? If he asks for an egg, will he give him a scorpion? Of course not! Jesus said, “how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?”

verse.text: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
verse.plain: God wants us to keep talking to Him and asking Him, because He is a good Father.

ask: What would you like to ask God for today?
talk.do: Knock on a door three times together. With each knock, say one thing to God: ask, seek, knock.
talk.pray: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thank You for always hearing me.

rightOrNot.text: Jesus' friends asked Him, “Lord, teach us to pray.”

rightOrNot.why: He needed bread for a visitor.

stories.title: The Father Who Ran
stories.note: The far country is shown by an empty purse and loneliness, not by the son's wild living.

panels.lambs: Jesus told a story. A young man took his money and left home.
panels.lions: Jesus told a story about a father and his two sons. The younger son asked his father for his share of the family's money, and went far away to another country.

panels.lambs: He spent all his money. Soon he had nothing left.
panels.lions: There he wasted his money until it was all gone. Then there was a famine, with no food in the land, and he had nothing to eat.

panels.lambs: He had to feed pigs, and he was very hungry.
panels.lions: The only job he could find was feeding pigs. He was so hungry that he wished he could eat the pigs' food, and nobody gave him anything.

panels.lambs: He said, “I will arise and go to my father.”
panels.lions: At last he thought of home. “I will arise and go to my father,” he said. He would say sorry, and ask to be one of his father's workers.

panels.lambs: His father saw him far away, and ran to hug him!
panels.lions: But when he was still a great way off, his father saw him, and ran to him, and hugged him and kissed him. His father was so glad to see him.

panels.lambs: The father had a party. “he was lost, and is found!”
panels.lions: The father called for the best robe, a ring and new shoes, and had a party. “For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found.” Only the older brother stayed outside, so the father went out to ask him in too.

verse.text: his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran
verse.plain: Jesus told this story to show that God is like this father: always glad when we come back to Him.

talk.do: Give each other a big welcome-home hug.
talk.pray: Dear God, thank You that You always welcome me back. Help me say sorry, and help me forgive others.

stories.title: Let the Children Come
stories.note: A gentle story throughout. “Suffer” is explained as an old word for “let”.

panels.lambs: Mothers and fathers brought their children to see Jesus.
panels.lions: One day mothers and fathers brought their young children to Jesus, so that He would touch them and bless them.

panels.lambs: But the disciples told them to go away.
panels.lions: But the disciples told them off, and tried to send them away.

panels.lambs: Jesus was not pleased with the disciples.
panels.lions: When Jesus saw it, He was much displeased with His disciples.

panels.lambs: Jesus said, “Suffer the little children to come unto me.” That means: let them come!
panels.lions: He said, “Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.” “Suffer” is an old word that means “let”.

panels.lambs: Jesus took the children up in His arms.
panels.lions: Then He took the children up in His arms.

panels.lambs: He put His hands on them and blessed them.
panels.lions: He put His hands on them, and blessed them. No child is too small for Jesus.

verse.text: Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not
verse.plain: Jesus wants children to come to Him. You are never too small for Jesus.

ask: How do you think the children felt when Jesus hugged them?
What would you like to tell Jesus today?

talk.pray: Dear Jesus, thank You that You love children. I want to come to You every day.

stories.title: When God Makes Everything New
stories.note: Told as a promise about the future, as Revelation tells it. No dates and no pictures of God.

panels.lambs: One day God will make everything new: a new heaven and a new earth.
panels.lions: God showed John, in a vision, what will happen one day. John saw “a new heaven and a new earth”. Everything old and broken had passed away.

panels.lambs: A shining city will come down from heaven.
panels.lions: He saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, shining like a precious jewel.

panels.lambs: No more crying, and no more hurting.
panels.lions: God will wipe away every tear. There will be no more crying and no more pain. God said, “Behold, I make all things new.”

panels.lambs: The city has gates of pearl and streets of gold.
panels.lions: Each of the city's twelve gates is made of one pearl, and its street is pure gold, as clear as glass.

panels.lambs: A river, “clear as crystal”, flows through the city.
panels.lions: “a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal” flows from the throne of God.

panels.lambs: The tree of life grows by the river, full of fruit.
panels.lions: On both sides of the river grows the tree of life, with twelve kinds of fruit, a new crop every month. God's people will live there with Him, happy for ever.

verse.text: God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes
verse.plain: One day God will make everything new, and there will be no more sadness.

ask: What do you think will be the best thing about the new world God makes?

talk.pray: Dear God, thank You that one day You will make everything new. Help me look forward to that day with joy.

list.verse: He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.

list.title: Don't Be Afraid, God Is With You
list.verse: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God.

list.title: This Is the Day God Made
list.verse: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.

list.title: God's Word Lights My Way
list.verse: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

list.title: I Can Do All Things Through Christ
list.verse: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.

list.title: Always Be Joyful in the Lord
list.verse: Rejoice in the Lord alway: and again I say, Rejoice.

list.title: Keep On Praying
list.verse: Pray without ceasing.

list.title: Love One Another
list.verse: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.

list.title: Be Kind to One Another
list.verse: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another.

list.title: With God All Things Are Possible
list.verse: With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.

list.title: God's Joy Makes Me Strong
list.verse: for the joy of the LORD is your strength.

list.title: Trust God with All Your Heart
list.verse: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

list.title: Let Your Light Shine
list.verse: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works.

list.title: Taste and See That God Is Good
list.verse: O taste and see that the LORD is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.

list.title: Walk by Faith, Not by Sight
list.verse: (For we walk by faith, not by sight:)

list.title: God's Mercy Is New Every Morning
list.verse: his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.

list.title: God Will Never Leave You
list.verse: I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.

list.title: Give All Your Worries to God
list.verse: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

list.title: Give Thanks, God Is Good
list.verse: O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.

list.title: A Happy Heart Is Good Medicine
list.verse: A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones.

list.title: God Is My Light
list.verse: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?

list.title: God Made Me Wonderfully
list.verse: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works

list.title: Put God First
list.verse: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

list.title: God Is My Safe Place
list.verse: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.

list.title: Be a Peacemaker
list.verse: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.

list.title: A Gentle Answer Calms Anger
list.verse: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

list.title: Love Your Neighbour
list.verse: And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

list.title: Love
list.verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,

list.title: Joy
list.verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,

list.title: Peace
list.verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,

list.title: Patience
list.verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,

list.title: Kindness
list.verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,

list.title: Goodness
list.verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,

list.title: Faithfulness
list.verse: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,

list.title: Gentleness
list.verse: Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.

list.title: Self-Control
list.verse: Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.

list.title: Noah Built the Ark
list.verse: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.

list.title: Abraham Trusted God's Promise
list.verse: Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them.

list.title: Joseph Forgave His Brothers
list.verse: But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.

list.title: Moses Led the Way Through the Sea
list.verse: Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD.

list.title: Miriam Sang for Joy
list.verse: And Miriam the prophetess … took a timbrel in her hand … And Miriam answered them, Sing ye to the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously.

list.title: Joshua Chose to Serve God
list.verse: but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.

list.title: Caleb Trusted God Fully
list.verse: Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.

list.title: Deborah Led with Courage
list.verse: And she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah … And Deborah said unto Barak, Up; for this is the day.

list.title: Gideon Won with 300
list.verse: and they cried, The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon.

list.title: Ruth Stayed Loyal
list.verse: for whither thou goest, I will go.

list.title: Hannah Prayed with All Her Heart
list.verse: For this child I prayed. … his mother made him a little coat.

list.title: Samuel Listened to God
list.verse: Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.

list.title: David Faced the Giant
list.verse: and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook … for the battle is the LORD's.

list.title: Elijah Stood Up for God
list.verse: Then the fire of the LORD fell … they said, The LORD, he is the God.

list.title: Esther Was Brave for Her People
list.verse: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?

list.title: Nehemiah Rebuilt the Wall
list.verse: And they said, Let us rise up and build.

list.title: Daniel Kept On Praying
list.verse: no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.

list.title: Three Friends Would Not Bow Down
list.verse: our God whom we serve is able to deliver us. … walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt.

list.title: Jonah Got a Second Chance
list.verse: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. … Salvation is of the LORD.

list.title: Zacchaeus Climbed Up to See Jesus
list.verse: and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him … Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down.

list.title: Peter Walked on Water
list.verse: he walked on the water … he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him.

list.title: Paul Never Gave Up
list.verse: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.

list.title: Sarah Laughed for Joy
list.verse: And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me.

list.title: Rebekah Watered the Camels
list.verse: I will draw water for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.

list.title: Jacob Dreamed of a Ladder to Heaven
list.verse: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest

list.title: Elisha Carried On God's Work
list.verse: I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me.

list.title: The Servant Girl Who Spoke Up
list.verse: a little maid; and she waited on Naaman's wife. And she said unto her mistress, Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy.

list.title: Josiah Became King at Eight
list.verse: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign … And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD

list.title: Dorcas Sewed Coats for Others
list.verse: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.

list.title: Lydia Listened with an Open Heart
list.verse: a seller of purple … whose heart the Lord opened

list.title: Barnabas Cheered Others On
list.verse: Barnabas, (which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation,)

list.title: Timothy Learned God's Word as a Child
list.verse: And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures
